'''Mikhail''' "'''Misha'''" '''Arkadyevich Shifman''' ({{langx|ru|Михаи́л Арка́дьевич Ши́фман}}; born 4 April 1949) is a theoretical [[physicist]] (high energy physics), formerly at the [[Institute for Theoretical and Experimental Physics]], [[Moscow]], {{as of|2007|alt=currently}} Ida Cohen Fine Professor of Theoretical Physics, [[William I. Fine Theoretical Physics Institute]], [[University of Minnesota]].

==Scientific contributions==
Shifman is known for a number of basic contributions to [[quantum chromodynamics]], the theory of strong interactions, and to understanding of supersymmetric gauge dynamics. The most important results due to M. Shifman are diverse and include (i) the discovery of the [[penguin diagram|penguin mechanism]] in the flavor-changing weak decays (1974);<ref>{{cite journal|author=Vainshtein, A.|author2=Zakharov, V.|author3=Shifman, M.|year=1975|title=A possible mechanism for the Δ T=1/2 rule in nonleptonic decays of strange particles|url=http://www.jetpletters.ac.ru/ps/1521/article_23274.pdf|journal=[[JETP Letters]]|volume=22|page=55|bibcode=1975JETPL..22...55V|archive-date=2011-09-29|access-date=2009-12-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110929221749/http://www.jetpletters.ac.ru/ps/1521/article_23274.pdf}}<br />{{cite journal|author1=Shifman, M.|author2=Vainshtein, A.|author3=Zakharov, V.|year=1977|title=Asymptotic freedom, light quarks and the origin of the Δ T=1/2 rule in the non-leptonic decays of strange particles|journal=[[Nuclear Physics B]]|volume=120|issue=2|page=316|doi=10.1016/0550-3213(77)90046-3|bibcode=1977NuPhB.120..316S}}<br />{{cite journal|author1=Shifman, M.|author2=Vainshtein, A.|author3=Zakharov, V.|year=1977|title=Nonleptonic decays of K mesons and hyperons|journal=[[Soviet Physics JETP]]|volume=45|page=670}}</ref> (ii) introduction of the [[gluon condensate]] and development of the [[SVZ sum rules]] relating properties of the low-lying hadronic states to the vacuum condensates (1979);<ref name=GC>{{cite journal|author1=Shifman, M.|author2=Vainshtein, A.|author3=Zakharov, V.|year=1979|title=QCD and resonance physics. theoretical foundations|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=147|issue=5|page=385|doi=10.1016/0550-3213(79)90022-1|bibcode=1979NuPhB.147..385S}}</ref> (iii) introduction of the invisible (aka KSVZ) [[axion]] (1980)<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Shifman, M.|author2=Vainshtein, A.|author3=Zakharov, V.|year=1980|title=Can confinement ensure natural CP invariance of strong interactions?|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=166|issue=3|page=493|doi=10.1016/0550-3213(80)90209-6|bibcode=1980NuPhB.166..493S}}</ref> (iv) first exact results in supersymmetric Yang–Mills theories (NSVZ beta function, gluino condensate,1983–1988);<ref>
{{cite journal|author1=Novikov, V.|author2=Shifman, M.|author3=Vainshtein, A.|author4=Zakharov, V.|year=1983|title=Exact Gell-Mann-Low function of supersymmetric Yang-Mills theories from instanton calculus|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=229|issue= 2|page=381|doi=10.1016/0550-3213(83)90338-3|bibcode=1983NuPhB.229..381N}}<br />{{cite journal|author1=Novikov, V.|author2=Shifman, M.|author3=Vainshtein, A.|author4=Zakharov, V.|year=1986|title=The beta function in supersymmetric gauge theories. Instantons versus traditional approach|journal=Physics Letters B|volume=166|issue=3|page=329|doi=10.1016/0370-2693(86)90810-5|bibcode=1986PhLB..166..329N}}<br />{{cite journal|author1=Shifman, M.|author2=Vainshtein, A.|year=1988|title=On gluino condensation in supersymmetric gauge theories with SU(N) and O(N) groups|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=296|issue=2|page=445|doi=10.1016/0550-3213(88)90680-3|bibcode=1988NuPhB.296..445S}}</ref> (v) heavy quark theory based on the [[operator product expansion]] (1985–1995);<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Shifman, M.|author2=Voloshin, M.|year=1987|journal=[[Soviet Journal of Nuclear Physics]]|volume=45|page=292}}<br />{{cite journal|author1=Shifman, M.|author2=Voloshin, M.|year=1988|journal=Soviet Journal of Nuclear Physics|volume=47|page=511}}<br />{{cite journal|author1=Bigi, I.|author2=Shifman, M.|author3=Uraltsev, N.|author4=Vainshtein, A.|year=1993|title=QCD predictions for lepton spectra in inclusive heavy flavor decays|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=71|issue=4|pages=496–499|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.71.496|pmid=10055291|bibcode=1993PhRvL..71..496B|arxiv=hep-ph/9304225|s2cid=14720093}}</ref> (vi) critical domain walls (D-brane analogs) in super-Yang-Mills (1996);<ref>
{{cite journal|author1=Dvali, G.|author2=Shifman, M.|year=1997|title=Full Length Article|journal=Physics Letters B|volume=396|page=64|doi=10.1016/S0370-2693(97)00131-7|bibcode=1997PhLB..396...64D|arxiv=hep-th/9612128}}</ref> (vii) non-perturbative (exact) [[planar equivalence]] between super-Yang–Mills and orientifold non-supersymmetric theories (2003);<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Armoni, A.|author2=Shifman, M.|author3=Veneziano, G.|year=2003|title=Exact results in non-supersymmetric large N orientifold field theories|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=667|issue=1–2|pages=170–182|doi=10.1016/S0550-3213(03)00538-8|arxiv=hep-th/0302163|bibcode=2003NuPhB.667..170A|s2cid=15435517}}</ref> (viii) non-Abelian flux tubes and confined monopoles (2004 till present).<ref>
{{cite journal|author1=Shifman, M.|author2=Yung, A.|year=2004|title=Non-Abelian string junctions as confined monopoles|journal=[[Physical Review D]]|volume=70|issue=4|article-number=045004|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.70.045004|arxiv=hep-th/0403149|bibcode=2004PhRvD..70d5004S|s2cid=118956344}}</ref> His paper with [[Arkady Vainshtein|A. Vainshtein]] and [[Valentin I. Zakharov|Zakharov]] on the [[SVZ sum rules]]<ref name=GC/> is among the all-time top cited papers in high-energy physics.

==Honors and awards==
Mikhail Shifman received the [[Humboldt Prize|Alexander-von-Humboldt Award]] in 1993, the [[Sakurai Prize]] in 1999, the Ida Cohen Fine Chair in Theoretical Physics<ref>[http://www.physics.umn.edu/people/shifman.html UMN BIO Physics Shifman] Retrieved April 28, 2019.</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://cse.umn.edu/r/honorary-professorships/#Endowed |title=UMN CSE Endowed Chairs and Professorship |access-date=2016-03-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160328092404/https://cse.umn.edu/r/honorary-professorships/#Endowed |archive-date=2016-03-28 }}</ref> and the Julius Edgar [[Lilienfeld Prize]] in 2006;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?first_nm=Mikhail&last_nm=Shifman&year=2006|title=2006 Julius Edgar Lilienfeld Prize Recipient|publisher=American Physical Society|access-date=April 28, 2019|archive-date=June 22, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190622155135/https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Shifman&first_nm=Mikhail&year=2006|url-status=live}}</ref> he is the 2007 laureate of the [[Blaise Pascal Chair]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.physics.umn.edu/about/news/news/242/Shifman_named_Blaise_Pascal_Chair.html|title=Shifman named Blaise Pascal Chair|publisher=University of Minnesota|access-date=April 28, 2019}}</ref> 2013 [[Pomeranchuk Prize]] and he was awarded the 2016 [[Dirac Medal (ICTP)|Dirac Medal and Prize]] of the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics|ICTP]].<ref name=aps>{{cite news|author=Gaal, Rachel|date=August 16, 2016|url=https://www.aps.org/publications/apsnews/updates/dirac-medal.cfm|title=APS Fellows Receive 2016 Dirac Medal and Prize|access-date=April 28, 2019|archive-date=August 4, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200804003847/https://www.aps.org/publications/apsnews/updates/dirac-medal.cfm|url-status=live}}</ref> In May 2018, M. Shifman was elected to the US [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://cse.umn.edu/college/news/cse-professor-mikhail-shifman-elected-national-academy-sciences|title=CSE professor Mikhail Shifman elected to the National Academy of Sciences|publisher=University of Minnesota|date=May 3, 2018|access-date=April 28, 2019}}</ref> 2022: Fulbright Distinguished Scholar. In 2024, Mikhail Shifman was appointed as the University of Minnesota Regents Professor. He is also a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref name=aps/>

== Political positions ==
In February-March 2022, he signed two open letters by Russian scientists condemning the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://t-invariant.org/2022/02/we-are-against-war/ |title=Открытое письмо российских учёных и научных журналистов против войны с Украиной |date=24 February 2022 |access-date=2 April 2022 |language=ru |trans-title=An open letter from Russian scientists and scientific journalist against the war in Ukraine |archive-date=25 April 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220425063900/https://t-invariant.org/2022/02/we-are-against-war/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://cse.umn.edu/ftpi?fbclid=IwAR3tUGb6J_4wdyvQQpUPM_c0rnXn7B1H12UxIxuUK3GSl18-6Yed7ROLe7g |title=An open letter to the Physics Community from physicists of Russian descent |access-date=2022-04-05 |archive-date=2024-04-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240408103833/https://cse.umn.edu/ftpi?fbclid=IwAR3tUGb6J_4wdyvQQpUPM_c0rnXn7B1H12UxIxuUK3GSl18-6Yed7ROLe7g |url-status=live }}</ref>
